verdict.tagline: A dark, twisting deck-builder that constantly reinvents itself.
for_you_if: you enjoy blending card strategy with puzzles
you like campaigns that shift styles completely
you want a deep roguelike mode after finishing

you prefer consistent mechanics throughout an entire campaign
you find initial learning curves confusing

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: A mix of card-based strategy and dark horror themes gives way to dramatic style shifts and steep initial learning curves.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a mix of card-based strategy, puzzle solving, and escape room elements.

citations.review_text: A card strategy game with mystery, horror elements, story; and a suprisinly large amount of depth.
Modern classic for a reason. The horror, escape room elements, and card game elements blend together seamlessly to create and utterly unique experience. Can't recommend enough

This game is a trip. At one point I turned one of my files into a card. I still don't know if it was bluffing about deleting it if the card died. It's wild. It's got a story that has me hooked (I haven't finished it yet), and the card game is genuinely fun to play – there are so many spins and variations on it that practically every battle is a puzzle to be solved. (Not to mention the other puzzles scattered throughout the various areas you explore.) I can't say much more without spoilers, but I [i]can[/i] recommend this game.
Interesting mix of puzzles & deck building, creepy characters/story, and escape room.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game changes style significantly after the first act, transitioning into different gameplay or visual formats.

citations.review_text: The marketing for this game on Steam should not be allowed. What you see is only the first few hours, and everything that comes after is a completely different, and much worse, game. Past the first act, all the charm disappears, all the fun evaporates, and you're left with an uninspired and un-fun fight against the most luck-reliant rng "deck builder" imaginable. The developer should be ashamed of pulling off such a rug-pull, and their marketing is scummy and unethical.
A friend recommended this to me, and after playing it and experiencing how much the game changes, I’d recommend it to everyone else as well.

Without getting into any spoilers, the game starts off very strong with an immersive dark theme, but then decides to abandon its strongest suit completely and switch to a goofy 4th wall breaking premise.

The gameplay itself was interesting at first and was genuinely challenging, but then got progressively more trivial to the point of acting as merely filler in-between plot points. 

I don't even think it is fair to categorise the game as rogue-like beyond the first Act, as it does end up becoming mostly pre-determined. 

All-in-all, I think had the game ended sooner, it would've been better. But as it stands, it lost me somewhere in the middle and I wouldn't say it was worth my time.
wish i knew the game turned into undertale/pokemon 8 hours in

I will be honest, I didn't finish it. The first act of the game is some of the most interesting, subversive & creative gameplay I've ever experienced. However once you finish it, the game transitions into a style of gameplay & visuals more similar to boring, tedious grindy RPGS that I personally have absolutely no interest in as a busy adult. And apparently, from everything I've read online, it never recovers or switches back to a more interesting form of gameplay from that point. Which is deeply saddening. I wish that they had found a way to stick with the thick atmosphere & subversive style of rouge-lite gameplay that the first act establishes. As the game exists now, the gameplay of the second act onward feels like meaningless fluff to pad out your experience while the game delivers its narrative to you.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Distinct acts introduce shifting settings, styles, and perspectives as the campaign progresses.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features multiple distinct acts that change settings, styles, and opponents as the campaign progresses.

citations.review_text:
Inscryption is easily the most lopsided game I have ever played, and one of the most disappointing that I can remember.
The things this game does well, it does REALLY well. However, there is SO much wrong with this game, I'm overwhelmed by the idea of writing a review for it because I don't think I have it in me to list off so many failings. The best I can do without spoiling anything about the game is this: if you like card games and/or atmospheric and interesting indie games, you will LOVE Inscryption for a while. Then, if you have any semblance of taste or value for your own time, you will be let down over and over again. If this game was just what it is on the surface, it would be an easy 8.5/10. However, when taken as a whole, Inscryption simply doesn't deserve anything more than a 6 out of 10, and that's letting the strong parts of the game really drag its score up.

I would not recommend this game to most people, but some will definitely love it. I DO recommend Inscryption if any of the following are true: you really want to play a very cool and atmospheric card game and do not mind being really let down at some point, or you are a terminally online adult baby who bounces up and down and claps their little hands when someone says something like "liminal spaces" or "analog horror" or "haunted save files." If the latter is true, this game very well might be the peak of entertainment for you.

[spoiler] The game doesn't seem like it would be split into 3 acts, but it is. While you're playing it, the first act seems like it will be the entire game, and it's phenomenal. The card game itself is incredibly satisfying, and the atmosphere is amazing. It will be fun for a long, long time while playing it, but eventually you will progress to act 2 of 3.
From here on out, the game will never be fun or interesting or tasteful ever again. Any and all atmosphere and intrigue is replaced with embarrassing millennial humor and le epic gamer references. In addition to complete…

This is a really amazing game.
I first tried it a few years ago and thought the card game seemed a little weak, but after trying it again, I found the card game a lot more enjoyable.

On the negative side, the first act is by far the best, and I kind of wish they just kept that going or let you replay it over and over. The second act is pretty weak by comparison and the third feels like a less atmospheric rehash of the original. 
Not to say they aren't fun. Just that the game starts at its strongest.
I found myself interested in the in-game story of the competing scrybes, not quite as interested in the found footage part (though it is interesting).

I almost rage-quit forever when my computer spontaneously rebooted and corrupted the save. Due to the nature of the single save, this made the game literally unplayable. It would boot up with the fix, and the fix is not enough.

I finally learned that if this happens to you, you need to delete both the game save and backup save (view local files), and ALSO turn off the Steam cloud saves for the game. I guess you can start up the cloud save again after successfully beginning a new game, but why?

It looks like there is a kind of new game plus (Kaycee's Mod). Haven't played it yet, but I am all for more of this game. Hopefully it lets you start back inAct One.

What can I say to describe this experience.... Without a doubt the most entertaining and captivating game I've played. Absolutely fantastic and truly unique. Had me on the edge of my seat the whole ride. Thought I beat the game really early and all of a sudden, its a completely different style and it seems like- I'm in a completely different game? And it was barely the beginning? Phenomenal. I was intrigued the whole time through this complex world, confused of how it just kept changing setting-style-opponents without giving me an option! Only one thing to do, play the game. 

Very good writing and world building, let alone the gameplay. Very interesting card game and buffing your cards/deck was so so fun! The ways it was done was very ingenious as well, different with every 'person' in charge. Those who seemed like Dungeon Masters in a gruesome D&D campaign. I just finished it now and I'm gonna check what achievements I didn't get just to have an excuse to play again :P

Highly recommended for people who like card games, high stakes and the thrill the comes from a bit of horror. Gotta play it again for a true rating but for now from me: 4.5/5

cohorts.summary: Extended play reveals hidden secrets, ARG mysteries, and a dedicated roguelike mode.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes a post-game deck-building roguelike mode called Kaycee's Mod.

citations.review_text: With the addition of Kasey's Mod, I most certainly can say I'd recommend this game. The sheer amount of little interactions between the cards is fucking wild to me. With the Mod, you'd be hard pressed to run into the same run twice.

This is one of my favourite games ever I can't believe i hadn;t written a review up until now (I was waiting to 100% the game first and after I did I probably forgot). Very interesting gameplay and a unique story that unfolds in such way unlike most triple A or even indie games. I was skeptical at first but now there is not doubt I love this game. I really want a sequel of some sort although we are probably not getting a direct one. [spoiler] I mostly want a sequel because for the biggest part of the game we play a limited version of the game and only in act 2 we see the real INSCRYPTION and I think taht ahs potential for a full game with maybe even multiplayer although, I understand it wouldn't make much sense since the game got deleted in the end and a multiplayer RPG style game would be very hard to implement. [/spoiler]. Also Kaycee's mod was a very nice addition to add more gameplay hours. [spoiler] Another expansion like it in act 3 style would be much appreciated as well [/spoiler]

great game, first run through will take ~12 hours, but getting the secrets/achievements takes ~150 hours (though, I accidentally left it running in the background often, so YMMV). This is shorter than Balatro and Slay the Spire, and I probably won't replay it as much, since there is no mobile version. It also tends to lag my computer for some reason. 

This game kind of has two portions: one storyline piece divided into 3 acts, and a deck builder roguelike ("Kaycee's Mod") you unlock after finishing the storyline. Each act in the storyline does have a deck building roguelike as part of the game, though. 

The storyline piece is a lot better than Kaycee's Mod. The Mod could have an option with less animations/dialogue/etc. so that it's faster to complete runs. I also find it feels too easy to win even with all difficulty settings turned on. I guess that's the compromise you get when you want to have a storyline/campaign kind of mode in a roguelike game - it can't be as difficult to win a run if you are meant to actually progress to other storylines. 

Complaints aside, I thought this was such a creative game and I'm glad to have been introduced to it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features hidden puzzles, secrets, and an ARG-style mystery outside of normal progression.

citations.review_text:
This is the type of game that will keep you on your toes. I'm normally not one for card games or needing to strategize my next move, but this game changed it for me. The gameplay is pretty simple throughout all the Acts, but it doesn't make the game easier to beat or the secrets easier to find. To not spoil anything, the amount of information you can find within the game itself is astonishing. It feels even more meta when you look into the ARG and while I definitely wouldn't have been one of the smart people to contribute, I couldn't help but feel on the edge of my seat learning more and more about the hidden story behind the story.

If you like games that advert your expectations, this is the game to play. If you like games that have tons of free mods to add in for more fun after, this is the game for you. And if you like a story that never stops giving, this is the game for you.

10/10: Youtube ARG the game. It is a game, and a game inside a game, and a game outside a game. 

Inscryption is many things, and many things it doesn't TELL YOU. At its core it is an addicting and extremely fun card battler where the normal rules are... easily changed. "my cards are bigger than yours" will not save you here, only your creativity and boundary pushing. It is a game where you are encouraged to break it at every turn, as Windette says "It likes to make you think you are cheating" but your dungeon master Leshy isn't above such tricks, why shouldn't you also use what he's given you to turn the scales against him.  

The fact that this game is so small and unknown is what makes it beautiful as there so many twists and turns that come as a COMPLETE surprise. I don't say this for many games, but this is a game worth playing completely blind. While you are made to think that they game you are playing is important, there is much more going on for those brave enough to look and follow the clues. It gives off a very ARG like vibe. 

If you like things like Deltarune's weird route, Omori, or other almost eldritch horror, or just love card battlers that through creative thought and hard work, can be absolutely twisted in your favor,  this game is 1000% for you.
A lot of fun, very interesting puzzles that can help but aren't needed to win. Also it is cool how many hidden interactions exist.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as featuring a main storyline split into acts alongside an unlockable roguelike deck builder mode known as Kaycee's Mod.

Even after you finish Inscryption, the post game (Kaycee's Mod) gives endless replayability as an enjoyable rogue-like deck builder that I keep coming back time and time again.

10/10 would recommend to anyone!
